**RICE AND BREAD**

[Verse 1]
I think this season’s been the hardest one,
Some days I barely saw the sun.
Counting every dollar, every crumb,
Wondering where the next one comes from.

Rice in the cupboard, bread on the plate,
Trying to make a little stretch and wait.
Some nights I cried when nobody knew,
But every morning I still made it through.

[Pre-Chorus]
I didn't have much, but I had a dream,
A little bit of hope still burning in me.
When everything said, “You can't go on,”
Something inside me whispered, “Hold on.”

[Chorus]
We lived on rice and bread,
With a thousand thoughts inside my head.
Some days I felt like I was barely alive,
But somehow I found a reason to survive.
No silver spoon, no easy road,
Just two tired hands carrying the load.
And if you ask me how I made it through,
I kept one little dream alive and grew.

[Verse 2]
There were days I wanted to disappear,
Days when the future wasn't very clear.
Bills on the table, fear at the door,
Wondering what tomorrow had in store.

But I learned that strength can whisper low,
It doesn't always roar when the hard times show.
Sometimes strength is making one more meal,
Sometimes it's simply saying, “I'm still here.”

[Pre-Chorus]
I didn't have much, but I had a song,
Something in my heart kept pulling me along.
Even when the whole world felt cold,
I knew my story wasn't over yet to be told.

[Chorus]
We lived on rice and bread,
With a thousand thoughts inside my head.
Some days I felt like I was barely alive,
But somehow I found a reason to survive.
No silver spoon, no easy road,
Just two tired hands carrying the load.
And if you ask me how I made it through,
I kept one little dream alive and grew.

[Bridge]
One day I'll look back from somewhere new,
At everything I survived and everything I knew.
I'll remember the cupboards, the tears, the nights,
And every tiny victory hidden out of sight.

I wasn't weak because I struggled to stand,
I was learning how to rebuild with my own hands.
And the woman who survived those days
Will be the woman who changes everything.

[Final Chorus]
We lived on rice and bread,
But we never let the dream go dead.
Through every hungry night and every tear,
I kept believing I'd get somewhere from here.
No silver spoon, no easy road,
But I carried more than I ever showed.
And if you ask me what those hard days said,
They taught me how to live on hope
When all I had was rice and bread.

[Outro]

Out where the dirt road ends and the creek runs slow,  
Boots and mud, coffee cups, tacos fallen, still we love.  
I got rough rocks in my pockets, mud caked on my boots,  
Life spills over, we just drink it up.  

Calloused hands from haulin’ hay, sun-kissed skin that don’t bruise,  
Chocolate with a squeeze of citrus, velvet with a wink.  
I’m a shy country girl, y’all, quiet when the world gets loud,  
Loving my big wife hips, kissing me quick like pickup sticks.  

But darlin’, underneath this grit, there’s a heart beatin’ proud,  
He tastes like midnight melted slow, cocoa words in a gentle flow.  
Says “You okay?” like warm rain falls,  
Wraps me up in caramel walls.  

Then night falls soft like rain on tin,  
Boots and mud, coffee cups, tacos on the pavement, we still show up.  
I shake off the day, let the wild wind win,  
On this dirt-road kitchen floor, we want less, we’re getting more.  

Slip between pink satin sheets, cool and slick against my skin,  
Sweet on my tongue, slow on the trust, silk and citrus, careful lust.  
Blushin’ like a fool thinkin’ ‘bout you slidin’ in,  
He’s cocoa heat with a lemon line, bittersweet and mostly mine.  

Rough rocks outside the door, mud tracks on the floor,  
He’s velvet voice and careful hands, drawing maps before he lands.  
But here in this glow, it’s all silk and more,  
Checks my pulse, steadies my spin, won’t dive deep till he’s sure he can swim.  

Reckon you’d like the contrast, cowboy—  
He’s chocolate sweet with a sour spark, golden honey with a question mark.  
The tough girl who wrestles the land,  
Sugar steady, citrus bright, soft by day, sharp by night—oh God, those hands.  

From muddy trails to satin dreams,  
He doesn’t drown in fantasy, he builds a bridge to get to me.  
That’s me, sugar—raw and real, with a side of sweet,  
Says I’m fire, says I shine, but tastes the edges of every line.  

Come warm these sheets… see what this shy heart keeps,  
He’s dessert that makes you think, dark rich love with a playful kink.  
If I’m sugar rushing through the dark,  
He’s the tart that wakes my heart.  

Boots and mud, coffee cups, tacos fallen but we’re turning up,  
Rough rocks, mud, pink satin sheets, come on, cowboy, fill my cup.  
He’s cocoa heat with a lemon line, bittersweet and mostly mine,  
From rough rocks outside my door  
To pink satin sheets and a caramel war—  
We rise up, turn up, drink it up,  
Love in boots and mud and a satin touch.

🎺 Big band: trumpets, trombones, saxophones, piano, bass and drums. Perfect for ballroom energy.For your song 🎷☕🍓

1930s Hollywood + Big Band Swing + Jazz Standard + Vaudeville

Think:

slow piano intro → sultry female vocal → upright bass → brushed drums → saxophone → trumpet section → huge swinging chorus → cheeky spoken outro.

That would give your “Satin & Pearls, 1930” song a proper vintage dance-hall personality rather than just putting modern pop lyrics over an old-fashioned sound.

🎙️ Jazz standard / torch song: slower, romantic vocals with lush orchestration.
🎻 Dance-band music: polished orchestras designed for dancing in hotels and ballrooms.
🪕 Country / hillbilly: acoustic guitar, fiddle, banjo and simple vocal arrangements.
🎹 Boogie-woogie: energetic piano-driven blues that became increasingly popular during the decade.
🎸 Blues: country blues and urban blues, often emotionally direct and rhythmically distinctive.
🎭 Vaudeville / music-hall: theatrical songs, comedy, character vocals and spoken sections.
🎬 Hollywood musical: glamorous orchestration, dramatic vocals and lavish dance numbers.
💃 Latin dance music: rumba, tango and related ballroom styles were popular in Western dance culture.
⛪ Gospel / spirituals: powerful vocal harmonies and call-and-response traditions.
For your song 🎷☕🍓
